    "solution.py": """"Write a python function to check whether the last element of given array is even or odd after performing an operation p times."""


def check_last(arr, n, p):
    """Return the parity of the last element after ``p`` operations.

    One operation replaces every element except the first by the sum of
    itself and its predecessor, using the values from before that
    operation. Hence, after ``p`` operations, the last element equals
    ``sum_k C(p, k) * arr[n - 1 - k]``. By Lucas' theorem, ``C(p, k)``
    is odd exactly when ``k`` is a bitwise submask of ``p``, so modulo
    two only those terms contribute.
    """
    values = list(arr) if arr is not None else []
    if n is not None:
        values = values[:max(int(n), 0)]
    if not values:
        return "EVEN"
    steps = max(int(p), 0) if p is not None else 0
    last_index = len(values) - 1
    limit = steps if steps < last_index else last_index
    parity = sum(
        values[last_index - k] % 2
        for k in range(limit + 1)
        if (k & steps) == k
    ) % 2
    return "ODD" if parity else "EVEN"

    assert solution.check_last([1, 1, 1, 4], 4, 1 << 40) == 'EVEN'

    assert solution.check_last([1, 0, 1, 0], 4, (1 << 40) - 1) == 'EVEN'
    assert solution.check_last([1, 0, 1, 1], 4, (1 << 40) - 1) == 'ODD'
